title: MirrorCheck
subtitle: AI-Assisted Impersonation Review
tagline: Turn suspected profile copies into reviewable evidence with Meta AI, local ML and contact redaction.
description:
A copied profile can look convincing long before anyone checks it. MirrorCheck turns suspected impersonation into evidence a human can review.

Inside an unofficial Instagram-style web prototype, a reporter uploads two profile screenshots. PaddleOCR extracts editable fields, imagededup and geometric feature matching look for reused photos, and local Presidio processing masks email and phone lines before Meta AI receives the images. The preview, provider-prepared image and saved reviewer evidence are checked for matching bytes.

Meta Muse Spark returns structured observations, differences, limitations and a recommendation. Separate local ML models estimate text reuse and auxiliary spam patterns. A default avatar cannot change the profile-model score by itself. No AI result adds a warning automatically.

A moderator must explain and explicitly confirm or dismiss the complaint. Version checks prevent stale decisions from overwriting newer reviews. Private history records the decision. A report-scoped, expiring appeal gives the affected party a way to explain context; the warning remains until a moderator upholds or overturns it.

We evaluated the new text model on 200 controlled test pairs derived from external professional bios, with source identities separated across splits: recall rose from 62% to 92%, with zero observed false positives among 100 negatives. On a separate Copydays photo-region challenge, recall rose from 2% to 36%, with zero observed false positives among 50 negatives. Difficult photo copies are still often missed. These research tasks do not establish real Instagram impersonation accuracy.

MirrorCheck runs locally with real Meta requests. Its prepared public-demo architecture isolates visitors, but public hosting is pending provisioning and verification. It does not connect to or modify Instagram, and screenshots cannot establish ownership.
short_description: MirrorCheck combines Meta Muse Spark, local ML, editable OCR, photo matching and contact redaction to review suspected profile copies. Explained moderator decisions, private history and scoped appeals keep humans responsible for warnings. Measured research challenges show improved recall; real Instagram accuracy and public hosting remain unverified.

answers.problem_and_users: Creators and ordinary users need a clear way to document a profile that appears to copy their identity. Reviewers need comparable evidence, visible uncertainty and a deliberate decision step. MirrorCheck targets that reporting and review workflow. It is a prototype of a potential social-platform feature, with no claim of user adoption or measured time savings.
answers.solution_and_workflow: A reporter supplies screenshots of the original and suspected copy. Editable OCR fields, image-region matches and masked previews help prepare the evidence. Meta AI provides structured visual observations; two local ML models provide separate text-reuse and profile-pattern signals. The report remains under review until a moderator takes an explicit action. Confirming the fictional case adds a warning that remains after reloading the profile.
answers.meta_model_usage: The backend calls the Meta Model API with muse-spark-1.3, using the English prompt version impersonation-evidence-v2-en. It sends processed profile screenshots, validates structured results and presents similarities, differences, limitations and a constrained recommendation. The API key stays on the server. This is visual evidence analysis rather than identity verification: Meta's recommendation cannot directly confirm a report. The demonstrated response is real and uncached; no Meta model was fine-tuned for this project.
answers.why_meta_matters: Meta Muse Spark adds a visual comparison that the numeric profile classifier cannot provide. It can describe reused biography text, avatar graphics, highlights and post grids together with meaningful differences and screenshot limitations. Local ML remains visible as independent evidence instead of being presented as a second opinion on identity. This makes the model output usable within a moderator's review process.
answers.technical_implementation: The application uses React, TypeScript and Vite, served with a same-origin FastAPI backend. Authenticated local workers run PaddleOCR, imagededup and Presidio. The provider boundary enforces image redaction; processed images are stored for authorized reviewer access. Logistic-regression inference uses JSON artifacts for the profile and pair models. Claims and moderator decisions persist in local JSON storage. The current storage and operational setup are suitable for a single-writer demonstration, not a production moderation service.
answers.distinctive_contribution: The contribution is the complete evidence workflow: editable extraction, image reuse signals, contact masking before the external visual model, structured Meta observations, independent ML and a separate moderator transition. The reviewer can inspect the same processed images used for Meta analysis. The profile model deliberately excludes avatar presence, and the interface discloses the pair model's synthetic training data. These are implemented behaviors rather than promised features.
answers.privacy_and_safety: A local OCR and Presidio pipeline identifies contact lines and covers them with padded opaque masks before provider image submission. Failed processing blocks the request. The demo verifies equality between preview, provider-prepared and reviewer-stored JPEG bytes, with no EXIF metadata in those processed images. Detection is imperfect: this is protection for detected identifiers, not a promise of complete anonymization. Reviewer evidence requires authentication. No screenshot or model score proves account ownership; the separate moderator action is demonstrated only on fictional accounts.
answers.challenges_and_tradeoffs: OCR can confuse handles, display names and biography lines, so the report form requires review and correction. A historical fake/spam classifier also answers a different question from copied-profile detection; the project separates those signals and adds a text-reuse pair model. Excluding avatar presence guarantees avatar invariance, but did not improve every metric on the older spam holdout. The synthetic pair model and screenshot-based evidence still require external validation.
answers.what_works_now: The English browser walkthrough records a complete fictional report, local inspection and contact masking, an uncached Meta Muse Spark response, local ML results, an under-review state, a moderator confirmation and a profile warning that persists after reload. Two example contact regions were masked; a second local OCR/Presidio scan found zero remaining detected identifier regions in those processed demo images. The most recent recorded full test run passed 123 backend and 24 frontend tests. These are development checks, not real-world accuracy measurements.
answers.what_is_next: First, build a consented, independently labelled evaluation set that includes legitimate look-alikes, fan and parody accounts, sparse profiles, changed usernames, image crops and OCR failures. Measure false positives and recall separately for copy detection and spam patterns. Then add verified ownership evidence, appeals, audit logs, database-backed concurrency, abuse controls, monitoring and a clearly defined deployment model. Any real Instagram integration would require a separate authorized integration path.
answers.open_source_components: PaddleOCR extracts text; imagededup compares image regions; Microsoft Presidio detects contact information for local masking; scikit-learn is used for training logistic-regression models; React, Vite and FastAPI power the web application. Embla Carousel and emoji-picker-react support the social interface. This source release includes two JSON inference artifacts and setup instructions. MIT covers original project code, with separate third-party and media notices. Raw historical training CSVs are not redistributed; the mirrored dataset's provenance and transformations still require review before other redistribution.

scenes.title: A clearer signal
scenes.voiceover: MirrorCheck gives familiar feeds a clearer signal. Our new landing page introduces the product with a moving gallery and liquid glass navigation. The goal is simple: turn suspected profile copies into evidence, while keeping the decision human.

scenes.title: Original and reported profile
scenes.voiceover: This is the original profile, and this is a new fictional copy. The display name, biography, avatar and photos are reused, while the username and profile statistics differ. Neither screenshot proves account ownership.

scenes.title: Report and review OCR
scenes.voiceover: From the suspected copy, I choose Report account, then Pretending to be someone else. I upload screenshots of both profiles. Paddle O C R extracts the visible names, biographies and counts. I compare those fields with the screenshots, correct anything misread, and acknowledge the review before submitting.

scenes.title: Privacy before Meta AI
scenes.voiceover: Privacy comes before the model request. Presidio detects the example contact details locally, and the server masks those regions in the images. I can inspect the exact processed previews. The moderator later sees the same processed evidence that was prepared for Meta AI.

scenes.title: Real Meta AI and separate ML
scenes.voiceover: Meta Muse Spark compares the processed screenshots through the backend. This is a real, fresh response from the recorded case. It returns visible similarities, differences, and a review recommendation. The interface separates Meta's visual score, the combined score, text reuse M L, and profile spam patterns. These are signals, not identity probabilities.

scenes.title: Human moderation
scenes.voiceover: The report remains under review until a moderator acts. In the protected review queue, I inspect the processed images, matching photo regions, the model's observations, and its limitations. Confirmation is a deliberate human action. Here, the moderator confirms this fictional copied account.

scenes.title: The saved profile warning
scenes.voiceover: The decision is saved on the server. I return to the reported profile and reload the page. The impersonation warning remains visible. An analysis score alone never creates this label; the moderator's saved decision does.

scenes.title: A report can be dismissed
scenes.voiceover: The opposite outcome is possible too. This earlier fictional report concerns an ordinary profile. The moderator dismissed it, and the account has no warning. Shared stock photographs can create visual overlap without establishing impersonation.

scenes.title: Clear limits
scenes.voiceover: MirrorCheck is a working local prototype. Its text model uses synthetic training pairs, and performance on real account copies still needs independent evaluation. Human review remains essential.

scenes.title: A second look
scenes.voiceover: Explore the prototype and both outcomes. MirrorCheck: a second look, a human decision.
